newsitem.title: USA: Port Authority of NY-NJ might delay bond sale.
newsitem.headline: Port Authority of NY-NJ might delay bond sale.

text.p: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey on Friday said that it might delay until the end of April a $920 million bond sale that it most recently expected to hold a couple of weeks or so earlier.
"We're now expecting to bring these to market before the end of April," said Allen Morrison, a spokesman for the Authority.

The bonds, which will pay for a new international arrivals building at John F. Kennedy Airport in the Borough of Queens in New York City, first were expected to be sold in the first quarter, but the sale was delayed until early to mid-April due to the complexity of the Authority's pact with the developer.
The same factor might push the sale date back a bit further.
"It's nothing terribly significant, except that it's a complicated agreement, and they're still dotting the i's and crossing the t's," Morrison said.
Lehman Brothers and Citibank were chosen to lead the underwriting when the bond sale was approved in November, 1996.
